- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >40% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–15% in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model overreacts; dampen forecast slope toward historical mean.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model delays adjustment; forecast should begin to converge toward true trend 2–3 days after sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates near end of period; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak observed in last 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history includes 3+ consecutive positive signals, model underestimates; increase forecast by 3–8% to align with sentiment momentum.
